definition.description: After a measured progressive build-in on a clear level lane, the athlete enters an upright near-maximal or maximal fly zone, runs through the marked zone, and uses a planned run-out to decelerate gradually. The exact profile declares build-in distance, fly-zone distance, intent, timing method, recovery, and high-speed exposure. This is not a static-start acceleration sprint, sprint-float-sprint, assisted sprint, wicket drill, or approach-to-takeoff task.

environment.surface: dry, level, non-slip running surface with a measured build-in, fly zone, and run-out
environment.space: one protected lane with enough build-in and gradual deceleration distance for the prescribed speed
inspection: lane separation and no cross traffic
footwear, weather, timing setup, and coach sightline
environment.changeRule: Changing fly-zone length, build-in, entry method, speed intent, surface, timing, assistance, resistance, run-out, recovery, or total exposure requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can build in and decelerate safely on the selected surface
current symptoms, recent high-speed exposure, lane, and recovery budget fit
understands the fly-zone, run-out, and stop signal
excludeOrEscalate: pain, limping, acute tightness, unsafe surface, insufficient run-out, weather, spacing, or communication conflict
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal build-in, fly-zone length, exposure cap, recovery duration, clearance threshold, or performance outcome

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 128 plus the focused max-velocity sprint research batch; Flying 10, 10m, and 20-unit zones are one identity with explicit dosage.

anatomy.laterality: alternating cyclic lower-limb contacts with reciprocal arm action
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, or guarantee performance transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate high-speed exposure when the exact lane, preparation, run-in, fly zone, and run-out fit the workout.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Build smoothly, run tall through the marked zone, and keep running into the planned run-out.
secondaryCues: use the marked build-in rather than rushing from cold
strike under your body without reaching
stay coordinated rather than forcing a universal stride shape
stop if mechanics, symptoms, or speed quality deteriorate
expectedSensations: brief high-intent effort followed by full recovery
unexpectedSensations: pain, hamstring or calf tightening, limping, dizziness, stumble, unsafe traction, or inability to decelerate
selfChecks: entered the fly zone under control
ran through rather than stopping at the marker
recovered fully enough to repeat quality

observationChecklist: lane spacing, surface, footwear, and run-out
contact rhythm, posture, arm-leg coordination, symptoms, and timing trend when used

faultCorrections.rushing_entry: lengthen or slow the build-in, rehearse, or use a lower-intent profile
faultCorrections.reaching_or_overstriding: reduce intensity or exposure and restore rhythm before another rep
faultCorrections.unsafe_deceleration: increase run-out or do not use the profile
faultCorrections.speed_decline: end the high-speed work or increase recovery

doNotUseWhen: a static-start acceleration, directional response, obstacle, assisted, resisted, or approach-takeoff task is intended
the lane, preparation, run-out, symptoms, recovery, or supervision is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved symptoms, unsafe lane conditions, repeated quality loss, or a mismatch between requested and exact profile.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Changing high-speed geometry, intent, surface, equipment, dose, or substitution reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, and validation.

sourceVariant.archiveReason: The legacy source lacks explicit fly-zone geometry, build-in, entry, timing, run-out, recovery, load, fatigue, and review contracts.

snapshot.description: Athlete uses a controlled build-in to sprint through a marked fly zone.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate short fly-zone maximal-velocity exposure after a controlled build-in.

dosage.countRule: count only a controlled build-in, one marked fly-zone pass, and planned run-out

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The athlete reaches the zone progressively, stays coordinated and upright without reaching, runs through the marker, decelerates gradually, reports no stop symptom, and retains stable timing or observed quality.
stopRules: stop for pain, tightness, limping, stumble, unsafe lane, or inability to decelerate
stop when mechanics or timing decline persists after full recovery
stop when recent high-speed exposure or session budget is exceeded
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Measure and inspect the lane, declare build-in/fly/run-out geometry, observe entry and zone mechanics, record quality or timing, and allow full recovery.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Build smoothly, run tall through the 10-unit zone, keep going into the run-out, recover fully, and report any symptom immediately.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate exposure to short upright high-speed running; no guaranteed outcome is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: shorten fly zone or build-in, lower intent, reduce repetitions, extend rest, or use a separately reviewed lower-speed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not add assistance, resistance, hurdles, a reactive choice, a takeoff, or more high-speed distance without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Smooth build-in, run through, use the run-out, and report symptoms.
supportPrompts.coach: Geometry, surface, quality, timing, and recovery are all part of the dose.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate longer fly-zone high-speed exposure with reduced repetitions and greater recovery demand.

dosage.countRule: count only a controlled build-in, one 20-unit fly-zone pass, and planned run-out

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: The longer high-speed zone stays coordinated from entry through exit, the athlete runs through the zone and run-out safely, and timing/mechanics do not show persistent decline.
stopRules: stop for any Flying 10 stop rule
stop when the longer exposure cannot retain upright coordination or recovery quality
stop instead of converting the work into fatigued conditioning
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Use only when the longer high-speed distance, recovery, recent exposure, lane, and run-out fit; reduce repetitions before accepting quality loss.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Build in smoothly, hold your best relaxed speed through the full zone, use the run-out, and take the full recovery.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate longer high-speed exposure; no guaranteed transfer or performance result is claimed.

doseScaling.reduce: use the 10-unit profile, reduce repetitions, lower intent, increase rest, or use another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not increase fly-zone length, reduce recovery, or add assistance/resistance automatically.

supportPrompts.athlete: Stay smooth through the whole zone, then take the run-out and full rest.
supportPrompts.coach: Longer fly zones raise exposure; protect quality before volume.

legacy.description: Progressive build-in sprint through a fly zone.
legacy.tempo: progressive build-in; high-speed fly; gradual run-out
legacy.loadNote: Bodyweight high-speed sprint exposure; exact fly zone and recovery are profile-specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate Flying Sprint with explicit 10- and 20-unit fly-zone profiles.
legacy.coachLanguage: Declare geometry, protect lane/run-out, observe quality, and preserve recovery.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Build smoothly, run through the zone, use the run-out, and stop for symptoms or lost quality.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact speed, lane, surface, run-out, symptoms, exposure, communication, and recovery context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: clear measured lane and gradual run-out
recent high-speed exposure and session budget fit
athlete understands run-through and stop signal
stopSigns: pain, tightening, limping, stumble, unsafe traction, lane conflict, or participant stop request
loss of upright coordination or persistent timing/quality decline
contraindications: symptom, unsafe lane, insufficient run-out, weather, communication, or exposure conflict
assisted, resisted, reactive, takeoff, obstacle, assessment, or conditioning intent without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute a static-start acceleration, sprint-float-sprint, assisted sprint, wicket drill, or long-jump approach.

score.reviewNotes: Candidate task-only reassessment from focused max-velocity evidence; independent calibration remains required.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact progressive-build-in Flying Sprint contract only.
